questions.problem:
The matrix $A$ and vectors ${b}_{1}$, ${b}_{2}$, ${b}_{3}$ are given below. Which of the vectors lie in $\text{Null}(A)?$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
A vector $b$ lies in $\text{Null}(A)$ if $Ab=0.$ So, we need to compute the product of $A$ and each of the given vectors and check whether it is equal to $0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A{b}_{1} & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=0\,✓ \\ A{b}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=-4\ne 0\,\times  \\ A{b}_{3} & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=4\ne 0\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, only ${b}_{1}$ lies in $\text{Null}(A).$

questions.problem: Consider the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}28 & -7 & 14 \\ -4 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}]$ and the vector $b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ k \\ -1\end{aligned}].$ Find the value of $k$ such that $b\in \text{Null}(A).$
questions.worked_solution:
If $b\in \text{Null}(A),$ then we must have $Ab=0.$ Substituting the given information, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Ab & =0 \\ [\begin{aligned}28 & -7 & 14 \\ -4 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ k \\ -1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-7k+14 \\ k-2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}-7k+14=0 \\ k-2=0\end{aligned}
$$

and for each of these equations, we obtain $k=2.$

We need to solve the equation $Ax=0.$ First, we find the row echelon form of $A$ as follows:

$$

$$

This corresponds to the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}+5{x}_{3}=0 \\ 0=0 \\ 0=0\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is ${x}_{1}$, and we have two free variables, ${x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}.$ That means we need to find ${x}_{1}$ in terms of ${x}_{2}$  and ${x}_{3}.$

From the first equation we get ${x}_{1}=2{x}_{2}-5{x}_{3},$ so the set of all the solutions of $Ax=0$ is

$$
\text{Null}(A)={[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{2}-5{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]\,:\,{x}_{2},{x}_{3}\in R}.
